precepts.text: Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God: whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation. The end of our conversation is leading us to New Jerusalem, that is soon to come.
precepts.point: As ye have been taught: some of the leadership from the old school went off, and the doctrine became that everything they taught was wrong, so throw it away and go back to Christianity. Did King Solomon go off? Do we rip out the book of Proverbs? Did King David go off? Do we rip out the book of Psalms? Men make mistakes, men do fall, but when they were in their prime they were teaching properly. You do not throw the baby away with the bath water.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
Colossians says to be stablished in the faith “as ye have been taught.” Hebrews says to remember those who taught you: “Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of God: whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation.”

Those who have the rule over you are the ones who have taught you the word of God. Follow their faith, considering the end of their conversation. The end of our conversation is leading us to New Jerusalem, which is soon to come.

That also speaks to what happened with the old school. Some of the leadership went off, and the doctrine became that everything they taught was wrong, so throw it away and go back to Christianity. Did King Solomon go off? Do we rip out the book of Proverbs and throw it in the garbage? Did King David go off? Do we rip out the book of Psalms? Shake that dumb black mentality. Men make mistakes and men do fall, but when they were in their prime they were teaching properly. You do not throw the baby out with the bath water.

precepts.text: The God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant. That's the blood of the covenant Zechariah speaks of.
precepts.point: The Lord their God shall save them in that day as the flock of his people: for they shall be as the stones of a crown, lifted up as an ensign upon his land. Not a brick, not cement: stones of a crown, rubies, jewels. That's how we're going to be.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
“As for thee also, by the blood of thy covenant I have sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit wherein is no water.” What is the blood of the covenant? Hebrews answers it: “Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant.”

That is the new covenant blood of Christ. The God of peace brought Christ, the great shepherd of the sheep, back from the dead through that blood, and by the same blood he sends forth his prisoners out of the pit. We are the prisoners. The pit is the same valley as Ezekiel 37, and that pit is Babylon the Great. It has “no water”: there is no truth in this land.

So Zechariah is speaking of our deliverance by Christ's blood. The great shepherd who was brought again from the dead is the one who brings the flock out, and in the end “the Lord their God shall save them in that day as the flock of his people.” All twelve tribes.

precepts.text: The blood of the everlasting covenant is Christ dying on the cross.
precepts.point: By the blood of thy covenant, the everlasting covenant of Christ's death, I have sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit wherein is no water: this is the pit, the valley of dry bones, and no water is no truth.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.why:
Zechariah says, “As for thee also, by the blood of thy covenant I have sent forth thy prisoners out of the pit wherein is no water.” What is the blood of thy covenant? Hebrews shows it: “Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant”.

The blood of the everlasting covenant is Christ dying on the cross. By that blood God sends forth his prisoners out of the pit.

If you didn't know it, this is the pit. Like it says, yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death; Ezekiel 37 calls America the valley of dry bones. This is the pit, and “no water” means there is no truth here.

Then Zechariah says, “Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope”. We are the prisoners of hope, and the stronghold is the Lord, this Bible: “The Lord is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble; and he knoweth them that trust in him.” By Christ's blood we are brought out of the pit to the stronghold.

precepts.text: If a man know not how to rule his own house: it is your job, not leadership's, to rule it.
precepts.point: Counsel is given twice on the same matter; if it is not fixed, both of you are wrong and you are wasting my time. Leadership gives the scriptures; it cannot make a husband love you or a wife respect you, and those who fix it never come back.

note.label: Trump Is Fulfilling God's Prophecy

precepts.why:
“Marriage is honourable in all.” Who makes a marriage honourable? Both sides applying the scriptures, the man and the woman loving their neighbour as themselves and dealing right with each other. A marriage does not become honourable just like that. Being an Israelite married to an Israelite sister does not make it honourable, because some are dishonourable brothers and dishonourable sisters: vessels to dishonour who hate each other, fight and argue all the time, speak evil about each other, with no love in the house. Those marriages are not honourable.

“For if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?” This is what the brothers have to understand. It is not up to leadership to rule you men or to rule your house for you. It is not our job to tell your wife to respect you. It is your job to rule your own damn house.

A lot of you come for counsel, and counsel is given twice on the same matter. If you are counselled twice and it isn’t fixed, you aren’t listening, you are wasting our time, and something is wrong with both of you. Couples come for advice, then a couple of months later: I hate you, I hope you die; and on the Sabbath, shalom, brother, Most High and Christ bless. You are fake and phony. Leaders, stop counselling the dishonourable, hateful brothers and sisters over and over; let them learn online, and deal with the people who really want help.

Leadership’s job is to give you the scriptures so you can fix yourself; it cannot fix you. We cannot force your husband to love you; it is up to you to be a good wife. And brothers, we cannot make your wife respect and love you; you have to figure out how to fix that. The ones who fix it never come back: the brother says yes, I understand, goes home and fixes it, and the sister fixes it. The key is that people have to see their own faults. Some are always looking for somebody to blame, and they will blame leadership, but ruling the house is the man’s charge.

precepts.text: Where no counsel is the people fall, but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.
precepts.point: No brothers counsel the women: senior sisters deal with the sisters and bring matters to leadership when they need judgment; that is the protocol.

note.label: Why Do Fools Fall In Love

precepts.why:
“Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls.” Watching for your souls is a job. Leadership is not about sitting in the front and getting the plates first. There are things you never see, never hear about and never have to deal with, because there are things put in place: the men who deal with the men, whose phones are the first ones to get called, and the senior sisters who deal with the sisters.

“Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.” If you don’t follow counsel, you will fall. A congregation without counsel will fall; there is no way around it.

You have all the wisdom and understanding in front of you. If something is said to you on the phone, you can say hold on, I’ll call you right back, and reach out to a senior brother or senior sister: does this sound right? And they will tell you: no, that doesn’t sound right; no, you can’t do that; no, that’s not wise. You can alleviate a lot of situations that way. But for some reason everybody is grown: oh, I can deal with it. No, you are not in your right mind, obviously. Because of lust you ignore all the red flags, and every red flag you see before you get married is heightened a thousand times after, because you are with them every single day.

The protocol is part of that safety. No brothers should be dealing with the women on any counseling basis. The senior sisters are set up to deal with the women, and if it is a congregational issue, or somebody has to be judged, the senior sisters bring it to leadership and it is dealt with there. That multitude of counsellors is how leadership watches for your soul.

precepts.text: Do nothing without advice, and when thou hast once done, repent not.
precepts.point: No brothers counsel the women: senior sisters deal with the sisters and bring matters to leadership when they need judgment; that is the protocol.

note.label: Why Do Fools Fall In Love

precepts.why:
“Do nothing without advice; and when thou hast once done, repent not.” The ones who watch for your souls give the counsel, and you are not to move without it. Sisters, you have been given the blueprint, the things to look for when it comes to men.

When looking for a husband, you are trying to identify stability and discipline. “He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls.” He is not stable; how is he going to take care of you? He is blown about with every wind of doctrine, bringing out little dumb breakdowns that did not come from leadership, like mashed potatoes on the Passover. Red flag. “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways”: one minute it’s this, the next minute it’s that. Spiritually you should never aim down; aim up for a man with more understanding than you, who can lead and guide you. If you marry a novice and you are the one teaching him to wear fringes every day, you lose respect for him, and you have married down. And don’t think you are going to change him; men typically do not look to you for counsel.

“But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.” A brother barely able to feed himself, getting kicked out of apartments, lights cut off, staying at his cousin’s house, is not ready for a wife, and you are not stepping in to save a negro. Spot the signs of lust: a brother telling you at 11 p.m. that he is naked is setting the mood and lining you up. Get the hell off the phone and put him in his place. And ask leadership how he handles correction: “he that hateth reproof is brutish”, and a man who cannot take correction from the men over him has a problem with God.

If you see these signs early, congratulations, sister, you spotted him. Now are you going to play dumb because you like the idea of being married, or wise up and follow counsel? Do nothing without advice, and once you have done it with advice, you will not have to repent of it. Break the cycle.

precepts.text: Blessed art thou, Simon Bar-jona; thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church. Great leaders empower others and make you believe in yourself, which is how the Bishop raises up bishops, deacons, captains, and soldiers by the thousands.
precepts.point: Think of the faith the Bishop had to have for the truth to be where it is. The impact reaches beyond the purple and gold: outsiders email to donate to the booster club, and every camp watches IUIC at 6 on Saturday night whatever time they teach themselves.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
Christ answered Peter, “Blessed art thou, Simon Bar–jona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.” Then he told him, “thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.”

How do you think that made Peter feel? Christ telling you, I am going to build my church upon you. That is what great leaders do. Good leaders make you believe in them; great leaders make you believe in you. They empower others, they strengthen others, they make you believe in yourself and not in them.

That is how a leader transfers his belief onto others, the faith Hebrews 13:7 tells us to follow. It is how the Bishop is able to raise up other bishops, raise up deacons, raise up captains, and soldiers by the thousands. Great leaders raise up more leaders.

precepts.text: Moses could not cross over, but was told to charge Joshua, encourage him, and strengthen him, for he shall go over before this people. Your job is to encourage and strengthen the men around you.
precepts.point: Think of the faith the Bishop had to have for the truth to be where it is. The impact reaches beyond the purple and gold: outsiders email to donate to the booster club, and every camp watches IUIC at 6 on Saturday night whatever time they teach themselves.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
Moses prayed, “I pray thee, let me go over, and see the good land that is beyond Jordan, that goodly mountain, and Lebanon. But the Lord was wroth with me for your sakes, and would not hear me”. He was told, “Let it suffice thee; speak no more unto me of this matter”, and to go up to the top of Pisgah and behold the land with his eyes, “for thou shalt not go over this Jordan.”

Moses could not cross over, but look at what he was charged to do: “But charge Joshua, and encourage him, and strengthen him: for he shall go over before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land which thou shalt see.” Charge him, encourage him, strengthen him.

That is your job as a leader: to encourage and strengthen the men around you. A leader transfers his belief onto the next man, so that the one coming after him can lead the people into what he himself was given to see. That is part of the faith that those who have the rule over you pass on.

precepts.text: Thou hast instructed many and strengthened the weak hands. Build the brothers and sisters up in the spirit.
precepts.point: Think of the faith the Bishop had to have for the truth to be where it is. The impact reaches beyond the purple and gold: outsiders email to donate to the booster club, and every camp watches IUIC at 6 on Saturday night whatever time they teach themselves.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
“Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands.” Your job as a leader is to instruct many. And your job is to strengthen the weak hands.

It is your job to build the brothers and the sisters up in the spirit. That is part of how a leader transfers his belief onto others: those who have the rule over you and have spoken unto you the word of God instruct you, and when your hands are weak they strengthen them, so that you can follow their faith.

precepts.text: When thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.
precepts.point: Think of the faith the Bishop had to have for the truth to be where it is. The impact reaches beyond the purple and gold: outsiders email to donate to the booster club, and every camp watches IUIC at 6 on Saturday night whatever time they teach themselves.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
Christ told Peter, “But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.” When you convert, strengthen your brothers. That is the charge that goes with the faith that is passed on to you.

Read on and Peter answers, “Lord, I am ready to go with thee, both into prison, and to death”, and Christ answers that before the cock crows Peter will thrice deny that he knows him. Christ prayed that Peter's faith would not fail, knowing what was coming, and still gave him the work of strengthening his brethren.

This is the leader transferring his belief onto others. Christ imparted his faith to Peter, and Peter was to impart it to the brethren. The one who has been strengthened turns around and strengthens the next man.

precepts.text: Paul went over Galatia and Phrygia strengthening all the disciples. A captain just back from Guyana reports the brothers and sisters there growing tremendously.
precepts.point: Think of the faith the Bishop had to have for the truth to be where it is. The impact reaches beyond the purple and gold: outsiders email to donate to the booster club, and every camp watches IUIC at 6 on Saturday night whatever time they teach themselves.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
“And after he had spent some time there, he departed, and went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.” Paul went country to country strengthening all the disciples. That is the job of a leader, and it shows how a leader transfers his belief onto others.

The same work goes on today. As the bishops and the deacons trailblazed the way, the captains follow the same path, and when they go to these places they continue to build our people up worldwide. A captain just back from Guyana reports that the brothers and sisters there in South America are growing tremendously, doing real good. The Lord has good things for them.

Like Paul in Galatia and Phrygia, the leaders go out to the nations where our people are and strengthen the disciples there.

precepts.text: The Lord stood with me and strengthened me. You get weak, need counsel, need to vent; a leader is there to strengthen you.
precepts.point: Think of the faith the Bishop had to have for the truth to be where it is. The impact reaches beyond the purple and gold: outsiders email to donate to the booster club, and every camp watches IUIC at 6 on Saturday night whatever time they teach themselves.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
“Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known”. The Lord stood with Paul and strengthened him, so that the preaching might go forth by him.

That is our job: we must strengthen one another. You get weak at different times. You need counsel. You need some exhortation. You have to vent sometimes. And it is your job as a leader to be there to strengthen each other, as the Lord stood with Paul.

So those who have the rule over you and speak the word of God unto you are there to strengthen you, and when you are strengthened, you follow their faith and do the same for those around you.

precepts.text: Uzziel and Hananiah repaired their sections, and next to them Rephaiah, ruler of the half part of Jerusalem, a supervisor over an area. Offices have leads entrusted with more. If you are overwhelmed for the Lord, that is a beautiful stress; ask for more laborers and pray and fast for them rather than complain, because the Lord put you in that office.
precepts.point: Think of the faith the Bishop had to have for the truth to be where it is. The impact reaches beyond the purple and gold: outsiders email to donate to the booster club, and every camp watches IUIC at 6 on Saturday night whatever time they teach themselves.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
This is the rebuilding of Jerusalem. “Next unto him repaired Uzziel the son of Harhaiah, of the goldsmiths. Next unto him also repaired Hananiah the son of one of the apothecaries, and they fortified Jerusalem unto the broad wall.” Each man repaired his own section of the wall. Then: “And next unto them repaired Rephaiah the son of Hur, the ruler of the half part of Jerusalem.” The ruler of the half part: he was a supervisor over that area.

That is leadership. When you come in the truth you may just edit the video, go on the fly mission, or work in the kitchen. At some point you become over the office: now you are over the brothers that are editing, over the IT team, over the building team, over the sisters. Now your job changes, because you have people under you. Everybody is not built for that level. You are not in charge; you are responsible for those in your charge. In IUIC there are different offices with leads in place, and a man who was once responsible for one office, the Lord entrusted him with more.

Sometimes brothers get overwhelmed, and that will happen. But there is no better thing than to be overwhelmed for the Lord. You do not have a demon on your back, you are not behind bars, you are not suffering illness; you are stressed out for the Lord's work, and that is a beautiful thing. So do not complain. Come up and say, I need more assistance in this office. Pray and fast for more laborers, and rejoice in it, because the Lord gave you that office and put you in that position.

precepts.text: Obey them that have the rule over you. So the Bible says obey them that have the rule over you. Plain and simple. And submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls. For these people watch for our souls. Even though in the past, when you were not in the truth, your parents watched out for your life and your safety and well-being, even though before they knew the truth. They cared for you all up until the time where you were able to repent and now be a commandment-keeping Israelite. So have respect and honour for them.
precepts.point: The same way we have respect for our elders, for the men over us, or whoever you report to, you need to have that same respect or more for your parents as well too, because they brought you into this world.

note.label: Honor Thy Father & Thy Mother

precepts.why:
“He that feareth the Lord will honour his father, and will do service unto his parents, as to his masters.” The same respect you have for your boss, your employer, whoever gainfully employs you, the elders and the men over you, you should have for your parents and more, because they brought you into this world.

Hebrews says it plain and simple: “Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls”. These people watch for our souls.

Your parents did that too. Even in the past, before they or you knew the truth, they watched out for your life, your safety and your well-being. They cared for you all the way up to the time you were able to repent and become a commandment-keeping Israelite. So have respect and honour for them, and do service unto them as to your masters.

precepts.text: Be not carried about with divers and strange doctrines; the heart is established with grace, not with meats.
precepts.point: These ordinances belonged to the Levitical priesthood, and the doctrines that would put men back under pieces of that office today do not even keep what they claim; they sound right because they use scriptures strongly and confidently, but they are in error. Be not tossed to and fro with every wind of doctrine, nor carried about with strange doctrines; do not ever fall away from the Messiah.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

precepts.why:
“Be not carried about with divers and strange doctrines. For it is a good thing that the heart be established with grace; not with meats, which have not profited them that have been occupied therein.”

The consecration ram, the wave offering and the heave offering were meats of the Levitical priesthood. The heart is established with grace, not with those meats. Doctrines that would put men back under pieces of that office use the scriptures strongly and confidently, yet do not keep what they claim; do not be carried about with them, and do not ever fall away from the Messiah.

precepts.text: The bodies of the beasts are burned without the camp; wherefore Jesus also suffered without the gate; let us go forth unto him without the camp.
precepts.point: Hebrews draws the lesson: let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach. Put away the sacrifice as it was carried outside the temple, and come out unto Christ.

note.label: Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out

precepts.why:
Hebrews draws the lesson from the ashes carried without the camp: “the bodies of those beasts, whose blood is brought into the sanctuary by the high priest for sin, are burned without the camp. Wherefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people with his own blood, suffered without the gate.”

“Let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach. For here have we no continuing city, but we seek one to come.” Put away the sacrifice as it was carried outside the temple, and come out unto Christ, bearing his reproach.

precepts.text: Be not forgetful to entertain strangers, for thereby some have entertained angels unawares, just as Tobias in the book of Tobit entertained Raphael and did not know it until the angel revealed himself.
precepts.point: The angel greets him: the Lord is with thee, thou mighty man of valour. The Most High already saw the warrior in the man hiding wheat.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
Gideon did not know at first who was sitting under that oak. “Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.”

It is the same with Tobias in the book of Tobit, who entertained Raphael and did not know it until the angel revealed himself. An angel of the Lord came and sat in Ophrah, appeared to a man threshing wheat by the winepress, and spoke with him as a stranger might. That is why we are told to “Let brotherly love continue” and not to forget to entertain strangers.

precepts.text: Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled: but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge; there is no permission for rape anywhere in the word.
precepts.point: What we witnessed is rape, and the scripture is plain that rape is a sin worthy of death; marriage is the only honorable bed. Men out here calling themselves Israelites and teaching otherwise give Israelites a bad name; we preach the laws of the Most High.

note.label: Judges 19: The Levite's Concubine at Gibeah

precepts.why: “Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled: but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge.” Marriage is the only honorable bed; there is no permission for rape anywhere in the word. Men out here calling themselves Israelites and teaching otherwise give Israelites a bad name; we preach the laws of the Most High, and the law says the man that forces a woman shall die. What the men of Gibeah did to the concubine all the night until the morning is the very thing God will judge.

precepts.text: The God of peace brought again from the dead the Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep.
precepts.point: The northern and southern kingdoms are to be made one nation again under one king and one shepherd. The one king is Jesus Christ, called the throne of David because David ruled over all twelve tribes; David will be present but is not the king. The chief shepherd, the great shepherd, the good shepherd who lays down his life is Christ, and he gathers the elect from the four winds and brings them up out of the land.

note.label: 2 Samuel 7: The Covenant With the House of David

precepts.why:
“Now the God of peace, that brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant.”

The chief shepherd, the great shepherd, the good shepherd who lays down his life: all of it is Christ. The God of peace brought him again from the dead, and he is the one shepherd over Israel, made one nation again. That is what the Lord meant when he told David he had spoken of his house “for a great while to come.”

precepts.text: Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.
precepts.point: They walked and talked with him and did not know who he was, which is the plainest picture of what the epistle warns of.

note.label: Luke 24: The Resurrection and the Opening of the Scriptures

precepts.why:
Cleopas answers him as a stranger: “Art thou only a stranger in Jerusalem, and hast not known the things which are come to pass there in these days?” Then he rehearses the whole thing to the very man it happened to: how the chief priests and rulers delivered him to be condemned and crucified, “But we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel”, the third day, the women at the sepulchre, the vision of angels, the body not found.

They walked and talked with him and did not know who he was. That is the plainest picture of what the epistle warns of: “Let brotherly love continue. Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.” Cleopas and his companion entertained a stranger on the road, and the stranger was Christ himself. Treat the stranger with brotherly love, because you do not know who you are speaking with.

note.label: The Beauty in Civility the Cost of Immorality

precepts.why:
“Remember them which have the rule over you”. That's the goads again. Remember them, respect them, pray for them. This is hard work, praying for mercy for all of us, including ourselves, and making sure we administer proper judgment. “who have spoken unto you the word of God”. Those are the wise words that prick you. “whose faith follow”. The faith we believe in is with us, and we're with that faith.

“considering the end of their conversation.” Listen for godly discourse, how to keep your lives right. That's the conversation we want the sisters having. The bishops put pressure on their wives to make sure the sisters are being taught righteousness and direction. Sometimes a sister does something nobody knew she would do, just as brothers sometimes do something out of the blue. That happens, but we still have to make sure the conversations are godly. The pressure is to do what God said, for their benefit.

Yes, we're strict, damn it. Think where these girls, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen, twenty, would be without it: diseases, babies, no husband, through by twenty-six, finished by twenty-nine, looking like a sea hag by thirty-five. We've got to fight to bring them up right. That's why God put them under the man, and they don't need weak-ass men. Be men and understand your purpose to rule this earth. The women get the benefit of that rulership when they get in order.

note.label: The Beauty in Civility the Cost of Immorality

precepts.why:
“Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves”. They're giving you the goads, the scriptures that prick you into righteousness. Appreciate it. Think about the near misses: Slick Willie could have got between your legs, knocked you up, walked away, and made you hoe number seventeen, another notch on his belt. You've escaped that. Whatever your past was, you're a new creature here. Get yourself together now.

That's why we work hard to set up Daughters of Sarah, Ladies in Waiting, Titus 2, all these programs. We're making proper sisters, daughters, wives, and mothers, that necessary part of building this nation. We aren't getting there without you. You're vital. If we're this serious about you, be serious about yourselves.

“for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account”. That's the heaviness on the leaders, the shepherds with these goads. When something goes wrong, we ask whether we went off or failed to handle something properly. We make a diligent inquiry right down to why you first thought of doing it, who was in the room, what time of day it was. Get to the root. Track the behavioral traits so when the next brother or sister begins that way, we can intercept before they destroy themselves. Without the cause, you won't solve the problem.

“that they may do it with joy, and not with grief”. We must give an account for every one of you, whether in righteousness or wickedness. We want to say you came with problems, learned the scriptures, went through the programs, got married, got children and a job and career, and got your family together. Trials still come, but we can give a good account of how the commandments cleaned you up. We don't want to say you didn't study, couldn't stop watching porn, smoking crack, or alcoholism, didn't listen, and aren't here anymore. That's grief.

“for that is unprofitable for you.” You suffer if we have to give that account with grief. You didn't adhere to the pricks. We have to let you go, cut off that hand or arm, and give the account that you didn't want to repent. We have to go through this to get to civility. Immorality costs us generations, our minds, the kingdom. Leadership is aging; we have to raise the next generation of brothers and sisters to carry this work on.

Bishop Kenaia's class last week was on point: radicalize the youth. Radicalize them to be hot in this truth. Christ said, I'd rather you cold or hot. Revelation 3:15. You've got to be hot in this truth, not letting BS pass. Make your fathers, grandfathers, and elders proud. We were entrusted with this gospel and won't let it turn into lasciviousness. As I would say now, we would spiritually break your neck. But I really wish that we could do it physically. That's what I'm really trying to say without saying it. Because I really want you to be that damn afraid to bring foolishness toward the prophets of God. With this Bible you know the past and the future and can travel through all ages. God gave that to Jacob. I ain't letting some worm mess it up. The hell with you and your mama.

Radius: a straight line from the center to the circumference of a circle or sphere. That circumference is how far the center point extends, not beyond. Radical is going beyond that circle in your thinking. When white people call you radical, you're thinking beyond the mold they set for you. It's a dog on a leash that can only go around inside that distance. Break the chain and run beyond their control, and you're radical. Don't beg Mr. white man to put the leash back on.

Look at the despair, our sons hating themselves and killing their own brothers and sisters, knocking women up without fatherhood and telling them to get abortions. Christianity is the leash keeping black men from thinking like men. You can go beyond Christian thought without criminal activity. Christ is black; pick up your pants, dress like a man, clean yourself up. The world says you don't have to. The hell with that, we're teaching you to be proper men. That's curbing crime, debauchery, homosexual lives, and fornication.

We're not telling anybody to pick up weapons or do anything criminal. Don't be a coward condemning the brothers trying to save your people just to appease the enemy and get us back on that leash. We're not doing that.
